newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says not biased and must be in Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says not biased and must be in Mideast talks.

text.p: President Hosni Mubarak on Wednesday dismissed Israeli charges of bias toward Palestinians and said Egypt could not be excluded from Middle East peace talks.

Palestinian and Israeli officials had said on Tuesday Egypt's input in talks on a long-delayed Israeli handover of most of the West Bank city of Hebron to Palestinians has raised U.S. and Israeli ire. A senior Israeli official warned of "confrontation" between Israel and Egypt.
"These allegations that we are not balanced are not true," said Mubarak, whose nation in 1979 became the first Arab country to make peace with Israel.
"They want us to press on (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat to accept their proposals whether the public opinion in Palestine agreed to it or not or whether Mr. Arafat finds it feasible or not."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's aide Dore Gold was due in Cairo on Wednesday. The Israeli official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the visit was intended to avert a visit by Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa to mediate in the Hebron dispute.
"Egypt instigated the peace process and our presence does not need permission," Mubarak told reporters. " Egypt's role is there and you cannot live without it."
Mubarak said Israel had requested Moussa's trip during a European security summit in Lisbon earlier this month.

"They asked the foreign minister to come and see what could be done and we have discussed the issue with Mr. Arafat," Mubarak said. "So he (Netanyahu) sent Dore Gold to discuss it today. It is agreed upon."

Mubarak said the criticism of Egypt was aimed at the ears of Israelis: "I was shocked. It's bad after you have discussed something to then go home to Israel and say statements that are against all that you agreed upon."

Egyptian-Israeli relations have been strained since the election in May of Netanyahu, who has rejected the concept of exchanging occupied Arab land for peace that formed the basis of peace talks since 1991.
